input.quote: (a) Cooperation on Termination. On its resignation or termination, the Servicer will cooperate with the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in effecting (i) the termination of its rights and obligations under this Agreement and (ii) an orderly transition of such rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer.
input.rationale: Section 7.5 is a full transition-assistance and records-return clause running in our favour: the outgoing Servicer (Cellco) must cooperate in an orderly transition, and "[a]s soon as practicable after the effective date of its resignation or termination" must transfer all funds relating to the Receivables and "deliver to the Successor Servicer the Receivable Files and the accounts and records maintained by the Servicer" (p0344/p0346). Section 7.3 requires the Servicer to keep performing until a Successor Servicer accepts its engagement (or the stated termination date), which is an open-ended assistance period exceeding the preferred six months, and Section 7.5(c) puts all reasonable transition expenses on the resigning or terminated Servicer rather than on us at its then-current rates — both better than the playbook preferred position. There is no immediate-deletion or no-return risk (walk-away). Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording are noted only: delivery is "as soon as practicable" rather than a fixed 30 days, no machine-readable format is specified, and there is no post-transition deletion certification; Section 7.5(b) also carves out the Servicer's proprietary processes, models and software and items restricted by confidentiality or data-protection rules. These are proportionate in a securitization servicing transfer (and Section 3.12(b)/Exhibit A require continued cooperation and data-protection compliance), so we do not redline.
